_why: LIMEN's inputs are large third-party corpora and a pinned model, none of which can be tracked in git. Independence cannot mean 'the bytes ship inside the repository'; it must mean 'the project declares exactly what it needs, can verify it, and prefers its own copies over a sibling checkout'. This file is that declaration; scripts/check_inputs.py verifies it.
_sibling_rule: Where an input exists both inside this project and in a sibling directory, the search order puts THIS project's copy first. A lookup that works only because two trees happen to overlap is a lookup that breaks when either one moves, and it fails silently -- the output is correct and the reason is wrong.

corpus.name: 136M Keystrokes
corpus.citation: Dhakal, Feit, Kristensson & Oulasvirta, 'Observations on Typing from 136 Million Keystrokes', CHI 2018

participant_files.description: 168,593 participant files. LIMEN's science scripts (trans_aware, error_structure2, decisive_tests, pos_all_classes) read these DIRECTLY; the project never invokes the keystroke-observatory pipeline.

noise_evidence.name: Channel noise evidence corpora
noise_evidence._why: measure_noise_distributions.py measures substitution rates from three published error corpora. Each is small; all three live under external-data/.

birkbeck.description: Birkbeck spelling error corpus (missp.dat) -- the English substitution source.

jwtd.description: Japanese Word Typo Dataset (JWTD) -- the Japanese substitution source.

cscd.description: Chinese Spelling Check Dataset (CSCD) -- the Chinese substitution source.

instrument.name: laya
instrument._why: The measurement instrument. Already pinned with per-file sha256 in config/pin_laya.json; declared here so a single command reports every input's status.

laya_snapshot.description: The pinned model snapshot. The revision is an immutable commit sha, NOT a branch: Hub main had moved by the time this was pinned, and a run must not follow main.
